title: Board
description: Program real boards over USB / USB-C from Polari (brd arc): every register device as a BoardDefinition with its Road (track all, simulate few — the UNO first), USB adapters and programmer kinds as rows, cited datasheet facts, the two rules (USB from the host directly or via a known adapter; C / Verilog / SystemVerilog only) as selftests, and pol board detect over hwmap's scanner (brd-0, 2026-10-01); brd-1: the UNO end to end in plain C — gen around the AVR header, build (avr-gcc, sizes measured, refused past the cited limits), flash (DRY-RUN, a real run needs a detected board + --yes), the simavr twin at a pty, and the twin's measured object cost.

engines.name: avr-gcc
engines.note: C compiler for the UNO (gcc-avr + avr-libc; RULE 2: plain C, no Arduino core) — the prf-board-engines image or a local binary (brd-1)

engines.name: avrdude
engines.note: flasher to the UNO's Optiboot over USB-CDC (DRY-RUN by default; runs only on the host holding the port — local binary or the local image with the port mapped) — brd-1

engines.name: simavr
engines.note: the AVR twin (simavr:atmega328p) — run as polari-avr-twin from the prf-board-engines image (libsimavr + USART0↔TCP + ADC0 stimulus) — brd-1

requires.engines_note: resolved per engine through board.custom.board_engines (BOARD_ENGINES_URL → local binary → the local image BOARD_ENGINES_IMAGE (prf-board-engines:trixie, polari-rf-node/prf-board-engines) → topology provider board.engines → refusal naming the knob + image); flashing refuses a remote worker
